title: Childhood adversity and recovery
text:
Decades after the landmark ACE study (Adverse Childhood Experience, 1998) revealed how childhood trauma can fuel lifelong physical and mental illness, new research is shifting the focus from damage to resilience. The Healthy Outcomes from Positive Experiences (HOPE) framework shows that supportive relationships, safe environments, emotional growth, and social belonging can dramatically buffer — and even reverse — the long-term effects of adversity. Backed by dozens of studies, HOPE is now being adopted by pediatricians, schools, social services, and entire communities, notably in San Diego, reframing care around strengths rather than deficits and demonstrating that healing and healthy development remain possible well into adulthood.  As Dr. Sege continues his work, he’s more convinced than ever that the effects of child trauma need not last a lifetime.

“We’re perfectly capable of healing,” he said.

title: Direct-to-consumer testing: promise and limitations
text:
Well, this is a mixed bag, the growing movement towards direct-to-patient tests on demand (especially bood testing but I suspect other studies as well in the future consumer marketplace) with a healthcare providerin the loop. This may be ok for some people, but I worry about obvious problems (over testing, excessive worrying etc.). We are in a buyer beware consumerist society. I am not trying to be self serving to protect the profession as I understand we are likely not going back!

title: Hamnet and Shakespeare's world
text: Saw this in the local theater! Really creative fictional rendition of Shakespeare's life in the mid 1600s, loss of his son Hamnet to the Plague, and inspiration for the play Hamlet.  Acting was superb (artsy) and for those with interest in Shakespeare and having read Hamlet, there is a lot in this.  More than a high browed (snobby) view of the classics, it is mostly about nostalgia and familiarity that is moving (of course, the original content has withstood time!).
